item.title: All-out rescue efforts urged
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-27
All-out rescue efforts urged President Xi Jinping has ordered all-out rescue and relief efforts after a mudslide on Wednesday in Nepal caused heavy casualties and left many people missing at a border port in the Xizang autonomous region. Xi, who is also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the instruction after the mudslide struck the Gyirong border port, a major land port linking China and Nepal, in Shigatse at around 10:30 am, according to Xinhua News Agency. As of 8 pm on Wednesday, at least three people had been killed and 265 others remained missing, CCTV News quoted local authorities as saying. The president stressed that the top priority now is to make every possible effort to search for and rescue missing people, evacuate residents at risk and provide timely medical treatment to the injured. He also underlined efforts to strengthen monitoring and early warning, carry out rescue work in a scientific manner and prevent secondary disasters. Noting that the country is at a critical stage of flood control, Xi emphasized that all local authorities and relevant departments should prepare for worst-case scenarios and extreme situations, and earnestly implement measures for flood and typhoon prevention. They must also step up efforts to identify and defuse potential risks and hazards, resolutely prevent serious and major disasters and accidents, and effectively protect people's lives and property, he said. Premier Li Qiang has ordered prompt efforts to verify the number of people missing and affected, conduct all-out relief operations and evacuate people at risk. He urged the Foreign Ministry to strengthen communication and coordination with relevant countries to share information in a timely manner and work together to properly handle rescue and relief efforts. Vice-Premier Zhang Guoqing has led a team to the site to guide rescue and response efforts. Video footage released by China Central Television showed muddy water gushing, carrying tree branches and debris, and some buildings were buried as the mudslide struck. Meanwhile, the disaster has cut off roads, communication networks and power supplies at the border port area on the Chinese side, Xinhua reported. In the wake of the disaster, China has activated a Level-II emergency response for disaster relief and a Level-II emergency response for geological disasters, the second-highest in the country's four-tier emergency response system. Governments at all levels have responded with immediate measures, making every effort to carry out disaster relief as well as search and rescue operations. Three central government departments — the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Emergency Management and the National Development and Reform Commission — have altogether allocated 220 million yuan ($33 million) to support Xizang in carrying out emergency rescue and disaster relief work. The Ministry of Emergency Management has deployed 249 personnel from the national comprehensive fire and rescue force, along with 325 engineering rescue personnel from China Anneng Construction Group, PowerChina and other centrally administered State-owned enterprises. A total of 30,000 central relief items, including tents, stoves, clothing and quilts, folding beds and moisture-proof mats, have been sent to support the evacuation, resettlement and relief work. At the local level, as of Wednesday afternoon, the Xizang Fire and Rescue Corps had deployed 72 vehicles and 431 fire and rescue personnel at the site, equipped with rescue dogs, life detectors, assault boats and other rescue equipment. Five repair workers from the State Grid Xizang Electric Power Co — the first group of emergency power repair personnel to arrive at the site — rushed there with a medium-voltage power generator vehicle and two small emergency lamps, and started work to ensure basic power supply and lighting for nighttime rescue operations. The local meteorological bureau has forecast continued rainfall across the county of Gyirong from Wednesday evening through Sunday, warning of possible floods, landslides and other secondary disasters in low-lying areas.

item.title: Turning tech edges into growth engines
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-27
Turning tech edges into growth engines China will turn frontier technologies into new growth engines by putting emerging and future industries, artificial intelligence-enabled manufacturing and next-generation communications at the center of its 2026-30 industrial agenda, the country's industry regulator said on Wednesday. The approach is designed to turn technological breakthroughs into large-scale industrial applications and build an innovation-led modern industrial system during the country's 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-30), said Xin Guobin, vice-minister of industry and information technology, at a news conference in Beijing. According to Xin's ministry, integrated circuits, aerospace, biomedicine, the low-altitude economy, new energy storage and intelligent robots will be developed into emerging pillar industries. China will also foster future growth points including quantum technology, biomanufacturing, hydrogen and nuclear fusion energy, brain-computer interfaces, embodied intelligence and 6G. AI is expected to be a central link between frontier research and industrial upgrading. On the technological supply side, the ministry will support the research and development of key technologies such as high-end training chips and multimodal algorithms, and pursue breakthroughs in frontier technologies including brain-inspired intelligence and world models, Xin said. On the ecosystem front, high-standard AI open-source communities will be leveraged as key platforms to develop a group of high-quality open-source projects for AI-facilitated manufacturing, the senior official added. As new information and communications infrastructure provides another foundation for emerging industries, the country is also looking to push forward the development of next-generation communications and computing networks, and expand the industrial use of 5G and the industrial internet, according to the ministry. "6G will be a top priority during the 15th Five-Year Plan period," said Liu Yulin, head of the ministry's information and communications development department. The ministry will accelerate research on core 6G technologies, continue technical trials and standards development, and promote the maturation of the 6G industry and development of its ecosystem to lay the groundwork for commercialization, Liu added. Smaller firms will also be integral to the new-growth agenda. "Small and medium-sized enterprises are closely linked to technological innovation and industrial-chain resilience, as well as employment and people's livelihoods," Xin said. In this regard, the ministry will improve its tiered system for cultivating high-quality companies, foster specialized and innovative small and medium-sized enterprises, and develop more "little giant" firms and single-product champions in manufacturing. It will also provide greater support in digital services, talent, financing and data, while strengthening protections for intellectual property and mechanisms to prevent overdue payments. "A national plan promoting high-quality SME development will be released soon," Xin said, adding that the ministry will also establish the second phase of the national SME development fund, strengthen inclusive financing and listing support, and improve a nationwide service network for smaller businesses. The future-facing agenda is anchored in a manufacturing base that continued to expand during the 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021-25). China's manufacturing value-added rose from 26.5 trillion yuan in 2020 to 34.7 trillion yuan during the period, while its share of GDP remained about 25 percent, data showed.

item.title: China's major industrial firms post double-digit rise in profits
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-27
China's major industrial firms post double-digit rise in profits Profits at China's major industrial firms recorded solid growth through July, buoyed by rapid gains in electronics-related industries and high-tech manufacturing, official data showed on Thursday. From January to July, industrial enterprises with annual main business revenue of at least 20 million yuan ($2.93 million) saw their total profits rise 17.6 percent year-on-year to 4.58 trillion yuan, data from the National Bureau of Statistics showed. In July alone, profits at major industrial firms rose 11.2 percent from a year earlier. The double-digit growth in industrial profits, according to Yu Weining, a statistician with the bureau, was largely driven by robust earnings in electronics-related industries and high-tech manufacturing. "Artificial intelligence is being integrated more deeply across sectors, driving sustained growth in demand for computing power," Yu said, adding that stronger demand and rising prices for related products had translated into rapid profit growth across AI-related electronics industries. During the first seven months, profits in the electronics sector surged 110 percent from a year earlier, contributing 9.3 percentage points to overall profit growth among major industrial firms, NBS data showed. Profits at integrated circuit manufacturers, including makers of computing and memory chips, soared 1,850 percent year-on-year. Meanwhile, profits in high-tech manufacturing rose 50.1 percent year-on-year in the first seven months, adding 9.6 percentage points to overall industrial profit growth. In particular, profits in optical fiber manufacturing surged 468.4 percent, NBS data showed. Despite the strong profit growth, Yu cautioned that the industrial economy still faced a complex external environment and a persistent mismatch between strong supply and weak demand at home. Looking ahead, Yu called for greater efforts to expand domestic demand and improve supply, accelerate the upgrading of traditional industries, support the growth of emerging sectors and nurture future industries, ensuring a smooth transition between old and new growth drivers.

item.title: High-altitude glacier collapse in Nepal triggers deadly mudslide
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-27
High-altitude glacier collapse in Nepal triggers deadly mudslide The deadly mudslide that swept through a major China-Nepal border crossing was triggered by a high-altitude glacier collapse in Nepal, China's Ministry of Natural Resources said on Thursday, highlighting the growing risks posed by unstable mountain environments as the climate warms. The disaster occurred Wednesday morning on the Nepal side of the border, sending a torrent of ice, rocks, and debris toward Gyirong port in Gyirong county, a major land crossing linking China and Nepal in Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region. As of 8 am Thursday, two residents had been rescued, while three people were confirmed dead and 558 remained missing, according to the disaster command center in Gyirong. According to the ministry, the disaster began with a high-altitude glacier collapse in Nepal. The falling ice and rock traveled rapidly down a mountain slope, scouring loose glacial debris along its path and developing into a debris flow before entering the Gyirong Zangbo River and becoming a mudslide. "The flow then struck facilities at Gyirong Port before continuing downstream toward Nepal," said Guo Zhaocheng, director of the geological disaster investigation and monitoring center at the China Aero Geophysical Survey and Remote Sensing Center for Natural Resources. The debris flow generated by the glacier collapse traveled at about 50 meters per second. The extreme speed left people little time to react and allowed the flow to affect an area more than 20 kilometers from its source, contributing to the heavy losses. The standards and requirements for disaster prevention and infrastructure protection in the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau should be higher than those in inland areas, Guo said.

item.title: Low-altitude economy nears commercial horizon
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-27
Low-altitude economy nears commercial horizon Regulations, infrastructure and business models must keep pace with rapid tech advances, experts say China's low-altitude economy is entering a critical transition phase. New regulations, breakthroughs in electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft, expanding manufacturing capacity and growing market demand have pushed the emerging sector into the spotlight as a potential driver of new quality productive forces. Yet behind the ambitious trillion-yuan market forecasts and frequent technological milestones lies a fundamental challenge: transforming industrial strength and technological breakthroughs into sustainable commercial operations. China's revised Civil Aviation Law, which took effect on July 1, 2026, introduced a dedicated chapter on low-altitude economic development, providing a legal foundation for the sector's expansion. The new framework establishes classified airspace management for low-altitude zones below 300 meters and replaces some case-by-case approval procedures with more streamlined filing mechanisms for qualified flights. The regulatory shift is expected to help move the industry from scattered regional trials toward a more standardized development model. Along with the evolving regulatory environment, China has made notable progress in manned eVTOL commercialization, although most applications remain at an early demonstration stage. EHang's EH216-S — a pilotless passenger-carrying aerial vehicle — became the world's first eVTOL model to obtain type certification, air carrier certification and production certification from Chinese civil aviation authorities. The aircraft began commercial trials in Hefei, Anhui province, in August, allowing public reservations and flight experiences within designated demonstration zones. The milestone marked one of the earliest attempts globally to move autonomous passenger aircraft toward commercial operation. However, such services are still limited to specific parks and tourism routes rather than serving as a widespread urban air-mobility solution for daily commuting. Another example is Aridge, formerly known as Xpeng Aeroht, which highlights a different challenge facing the industry: strong manufacturing capabilities but incomplete commercialization conditions. In August, Aridge's flying car manufacturing base in Guangzhou, Guangdong province, produced its 1,000th set of 800-volt high-voltage electric propulsion units, demonstrating China's growing ability to manufacture key eVTOL components at scale. The company's modular Land Aircraft Carrier has completed a series of tests, including automatic separation, independent flight and docking between its ground vehicle and detachable aircraft cabin. It has attracted more than 7,000 global preorders and purchase intentions from individual consumers, government and enterprise customers, as well as overseas markets. However, the aircraft has not yet obtained the suitable certificate required for formal manned commercial operations and its planned mass deliveries remain dependent on the completion of airworthiness reviews.

item.title: UBS China: RMB key funding option for global institutions
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-27
UBS China head: RMB key funding option for global institutions UBS has priced its first ever panda bond, becoming the first Swiss financial institution to tap the onshore renminbi market, with a 1.78 percent coupon — the lowest on record for a five-year panda bond issued by a foreign financial institution. In an interview with China Perspective, Janice Hu, China country head of UBS AG, said the growing international connectivity, maturity and relevance of China's bond market have made it a natural funding market for international institutions. "We see the onshore RMB market as an important component of UBS's diversified funding toolkit," Hu said, adding that panda bonds and RMB financing can play an increasingly meaningful role as international institutions diversify their funding amid heightened global financial volatility. Zhu Jingyi and Wang Zhiyi contributed to this story.

item.description:

President Xi Jinping urges all-out rescue, relief efforts after mudslide hits border port in Xizang Level-II emergency response activated after mudslide hits border port in Xizang A second group of 29 civil aviation support personnel arrived at Dingri Airport in Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region, on Thursday afternoon to assist relief operations following the mudslide disaster in Gyirong county, according to the regional government. The team, dispatched by Xizang Airport Group and the regional air traffic control center, specialize in security checks, aircraft security, cargo handling, driving of special vehicles, supervision of loading and unloading, medical services, firefighting, communications and meteorological observation. Airport support vehicles have also been sent to Dingri and Shigatse Heping airports. Dingri Airport is the closest airport to Gyirong and using there can shorten transit time of supplies to the disaster-hit area by more than five hours compared with Heping Airport in Shigatse. Following the disaster, the regional civil aviation administration activated an emergency response mechanism and coordinated flight capacity, with Lhasa and Dingri airports serving as key transfer hubs for rescue personnel and supplies. So far, 37 support personnel have been dispatched. Airports in Xizang have handled seven emergency rescue flights, 31.8 metric tons of relief supplies and transported more than 300 rescue and relief personnel. Emergency telecommunications teams in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region have restored one damaged base station and deployed two new ones in the mudslide-affected Gyirong Port area in Gyirong county, Shigatse, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology said on Thursday. The National Health Commission said on Thursday that it has mobilized medical and psychological relief for areas in Xizang autonomous region affected by a devastating mudslide that struck the Gyirong border port on Wednesday morning. The commission said it has dispatched officials to Xizang to oversee medical rescue and emergency operations, and coordinated with regional authorities to deploy healthcare resources. Personnel from the People's Hospital of Xizang autonomous region and the regional center for disease control and prevention have been sent to affected areas, along with emergency supplies, disinfection materials and specialized vehicles. Ambulances, medical staff and psychological workers from Gyirong county and neighboring counties in Shigatse city have been dispatched to mudslide-hit areas to address frontline needs. Xizang has activated a 24-hour psychological assistance hotline, while additional hospitals have been put on standby, with blood supply support secured. Several national-level emergency medical rescue teams are also on standby to reinforce frontline care, while medical contingency work continues. China's Ministry of Water Resources said that a significant barrier lake has formed near the confluence of the Chhochen Khola and Purepu Tsangpo rivers in Nepal, with its water volume estimated at 2 million cubic meters as of Thursday morning and the lake already overflowing. The ministry said another 3 million cubic meters of water is expected to flow into the lake over the next three days, making the risk of a breach high, China Central Television quoted a source from the ministry as saying on Thursday. According to the source, the ministry is closely monitoring the lake's development and conducting calculations and analyses on a possible outburst flood to support emergency rescue and relief work. The lake formation comes after a landslide that began in Nepal on Wednesday morning and caused heavy casualties and large numbers of missing persons at Gyirong Port in Gyirong county, Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region. Three people had been confirmed killed, while 558 others remained missing, as of 8 am on Thursday after a mudslide struck the port along the China-Nepal border in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region, Xinhua News Agency reported. Two other villagers had been rescued. Among the missing, 260 have been identified as foreign nationals, according to Norbu Tsering, the first commander of the on-site headquarters, the report added. The deadly mudslide that swept through a major China-Nepal border crossing was triggered by a high-altitude glacier collapse in Nepal, China's Ministry of Natural Resources said on Thursday, highlighting the growing risks posed by unstable mountain environments as the climate warms. The disaster occurred Wednesday morning on the Nepal side of the border, sending a torrent of ice, rocks, and debris toward Gyirong port in Gyirong county, a major land crossing linking China and Nepal in Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region. As of 8 am Thursday, two residents had been rescued, while three people were confirmed dead and 558 remained missing, according to the disaster command center in Gyirong. According to the ministry, the disaster began with a high-altitude glacier collapse in Nepal. The falling ice and rock traveled rapidly down a mountain slope, scouring loose glacial debris along its path and developing into a debris flow before entering the Gyirong Zangbo River and becoming a mudslide. "The flow then struck facilities at Gyirong Port before continuing downstream toward Nepal," said Guo Zhaocheng, director of the geological disaster investigation and monitoring center at the China Aero Geophysical Survey and Remote Sensing Center for Natural Resources. The debris flow generated by the glacier collapse traveled at about 50 meters per second. The standards and requirements for disaster prevention and infrastructure protection in the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau should be higher than those in inland areas, Guo said. The central government's first round of emergency relief supplies for the victims of yesterday's landslide in the Xizang autonomous region arrived at a parking lot in Gyirong town at approximately 11 am on Thursday, according to Xizang TV. Rescue workers have already unloaded the first shipment of relief materials, and the supplies will be distributed to affected residents as soon as possible, the report said. The shipment includes 30,000 sets of items, including moisture-proof mats, tents, warm clothing, and heating stoves. Guo Xiaohong, Party chief and director of the Xizang Food and Strategic Reserves Administration, said the supplies had departed at 3:30 pm on Wednesday after the region received the central government's dispatch notice. "Additional vehicles are arriving successively," Guo was quoted as saying by Xizang TV. "At present, all types of relief materials, as well as grain and oil reserves, are fully stocked and adequately supplied." A mudslide in Nepal struck the Gyirong border port in Shigatse, Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region, cutting off roads and communication lines and burying some buildings. At 8:20 am Thursday, the Xizang Military Command urgently dispatched two helicopters to survey the disaster zone and plan rescue routes. Watch the video for the latest updates on the rescue efforts. GYIRONG, Xizang -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang arrived at Gyirong township in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region Thursday afternoon, after a massive mudslide hit the area Wednesday morning. Li, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, is entrusted by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, to lead a group of senior officials from relevant departments to the disaster-hit area. They will supervise rescue and relief operations, and visit rescue and relief personnel and people affected by the disaster. GYIRONG, Xizang -- Residents of villages near a border port struck by a mudslide in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region have all been evacuated, according to Xizang's border inspection authorities. The mudslide, which occurred on the Nepalese side, struck Gyirong Port in Gyirong county, Xizang, on Wednesday morning, leaving three people dead and 558 others, including 260 foreign nationals, missing, according to preliminary estimates. In the wake of the mudslide, over 300 villagers from several villages near the port, with the assistance of rescue forces of Xizang's border inspection authorities, have been evacuated to safe places in Gyirong county for their safety. Rescue forces from China Anneng Construction Group have been deployed to Gyirong county in Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region, to conduct emergency rescue operations at a local port. A severe mudslide has disrupted roads, communications, and power supplies. The mudslide, which occurred around 10:30 am Wednesday in Nepal, caused significant casualties after striking the Gyirong border port, a major land connection between China and Nepal in Shigatse. As of 8 am Thursday, the disaster has resulted in three deaths and 558 people reported missing. Following the disaster, China Anneng group, a State-owned engineering and rescue enterprise, activated its emergency response mechanism as directed by the Ministry of Emergency Management. A total of 310 technical experts and rescue personnel, including specialists in geology and engineering, were quickly mobilized from cities such as Beijing, Chengdu, Chongqing, and Lhasa, the group said. The rescue team brought with them 120 sets of advanced, purpose-built equipment, including multifunctional survey drones, 3D laser scanners, life-detection devices, large excavators, and loaders, as they rushed to the affected area for relief operations. The 310 rescuers and 120 sets of equipment are expected to arrive at the disaster site on Thursday afternoon, it said. An eight-member advance team from the group's engineering rescue base in Lhasa, equipped with communication and detection gear, arrived in the county early Thursday morning. Under the direction of the frontline rescue command center, the team has been tasked with advancing to the upstream barrier lake and conducting aerial surveys and 3D modeling using portable satellite stations, reconnaissance drones, and 3D laser scanners. The operation aims to gather key data, including the properties of surrounding rock, and the dam's dimensions and flow velocity, to provide scientific data support for subsequent barrier lake disposal efforts. The top priority, according to a frontline rescuer, is to neutralize the threat posed by the upstream barrier lake. Only once that danger is mitigated can safe conditions be established for clearing sediment accumulation approximately three kilometers upstream of the border crossing, it said. A national-level specialized comprehensive emergency response force has arrived in Gyirong county in Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region, to reinforce relief efforts after a mudslide that claimed three lives and left 558 others missing, Xinhua News Agency reported on Thursday. The China Search and Rescue Team arrived in the county at 2:28 pm on Thursday to bolster local emergency efforts and will continue advancing to the Gyirong border port, which has been more severely affected by the mudslide, to carry out rescue operations, the agency said. The mudslide in Nepal struck the Gyirong border port, a major land port linking China and Nepal in Shigatse, at around 10:30 am on Wednesday. As of 8 am on Thursday, it has left three dead and 558 missing, authorities said. GYIRONG -- The first team of 141 rescuers has arrived at the mudslide-stricken border port of Gyirong in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region on Thursday morning after the disaster caused significant casualties along the China-Nepal border, according to China's Ministry of Emergency Management. A high-altitude helicopter has also arrived at the disaster-hit area, the ministry said. The mudslide struck Gyirong Port in Gyirong county, Xizang, on Wednesday morning. As of 8 am on Thursday, three people had been killed, 558 others remained missing, while two local villagers had been rescued, local authorities said. Another batch of 111 rescuers from the China Search and Rescue team has arrived at Gyirong county as of 2:28 pm Thursday, and will head to Gyirong Port to carry out rescue operations. An eight-member advance team from China Anneng, a State-owned engineering and rescue enterprise, arrived in Gyirong county early Thursday with communications and detection equipment to collect key data and support efforts to address an upstream blockage, which is a top priority. Only after the risk posed by the blockage is addressed can the debris accumulated about 3 km upstream of the port be safely cleared, according to rescue personnel at the site. Hundreds more rescuers, carrying equipment and supplies for detection, rescue, communications and logistical support, are rushing to the site. The guidance team of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Western Theater Command arrived at a high-altitude airport in the Xizang autonomous region aboard a Y-20 transport aircraft at around 10:30 am on Thursday to join rescue efforts following a mudslide that struck Gyirong county in Shigatse on Wednesday. The guidance team then immediately traveled to the disaster site to strengthen command of the rescue operation. The Y-20 carrying the team took off on Thursday morning. The team will organize a joint rescue operation involving PLA personnel in Gyirong county. The Red Cross Society of China has sent a working group and relief supplies to regions affected by a mudslide that struck Gyirong border port in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region on Wednesday morning. The working group was sent on Wednesday evening, along with a total of 2,500 units of relief materials, including tents, family kits, hygiene packs, quilts, folding beds, and winter jackets. In addition, the Chinese Red Cross Foundation has provided more than 5,500 boxes of bottled water, instant noodles, ham sausages, and milk to support the temporary resettlement and basic living needs of affected communities. A 111-member elite fire and rescue team arrived in Dingri county, Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region, at around 8 am Thursday. They are en route by road to the worst-hit area after a mudslide disaster left three people dead and 558 others missing. Dispatched by the Ministry of Emergency Management and the National Fire and Rescue Administration, the team brought over 500 sets of equipment for detection, life-saving, demolition, communications, and medical support, along with four search-and-rescue dogs. The mudslide occurred at around 10:30 am Wednesday on the Nepalese side of the border, causing major casualties and missing persons at Gyirong port in Gyirong county, Shigatse. As of 8 am Thursday, two people had been rescued, three were confirmed dead, and the number of missing had been updated to 558, including 260 foreign nationals. The figures are still being verified, according to local authorities. In response, the Xizang regional disaster prevention, reduction, and relief commission activated a Level-I regional natural disaster relief emergency response, with rescue forces rapidly assembled and sent to the disaster site. On Aug 26, a mudslide in Nepal struck the Gyirong border port in Shigatse, Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region, cutting off roads and communication lines, with some buildings buried. The Shigatse detachment of the People's Armed Police Force Xizang Contingent quickly mobilized over 140 personnel with over 200 sets of rescue equipment to the disaster zone. Continuous rainfall brought secondary landslide risks, halting the advance of main forces and heavy equipment. Elite teams were dispatched to clear debris and reinforce slopes, racing to reopen vital roads. Rescuers are prepared for continuous operations. Once conditions allow, they will push into the core affected zone to search for the missing, evacuate stranded residents and prevent secondary hazards, in an all-out effort to safeguard people's lives and property. China's meteorological authorities upgraded their emergency response on Wednesday after a mudslide in Nepal caused major casualties and left hundreds missing at Gyirong Port in the Xizang autonomous region. The mudslide occurred on Wednesday morning on the Nepal side of the border, affecting Gyirong Port in Gyirong county, a major land crossing linking China and Nepal in Shigatse. As of 8 am, three people had been confirmed dead and 558 remained missing. On Wednesday evening, the China Meteorological Administration raised its emergency response for major meteorological disasters, including typhoons, torrential rain and severe convective weather, from Level III to Level II. The meteorological authorities will strengthen coordination, while combining high-resolution satellite remote sensing with meteorological monitoring data to identify potential secondary disaster risks around the mudslide-affected area, according to the administration. They will also continue to update weather forecasts and monitoring information to provide ongoing support for rescue and relief efforts. Following the disaster, the National Satellite Meteorological Center quickly set up a special response team and established a joint emergency support group with the Xizang regional meteorological observatory to provide technical assistance. Using the cloud platform of China's intelligent weather warning system, known as MAZU, Chinese meteorological authorities also held consultations with Nepalese meteorological departments and issued rapid updates on monitoring and forecasting severe weather worldwide. The National Satellite Meteorological Center analyzed satellite imagery of the affected area using data from the HJ-2 satellite, while the China Meteorological Data Service Center promptly prepared an emergency weather service bulletin to provide real-time data support for rescue operations. The administration's Meteorological Observation Center established a dedicated monitoring team, combining satellite-ground integrated products with ground observation data to assess changes in radar reflectivity and precipitation in the affected and upstream areas. As of Wednesday, meteorological authorities in Xizang had issued three special weather service reports for rescue and relief efforts, along with a satellite remote-sensing image product for the disaster area, according to the administration.
